title: Burst reserve negotiation and SLA decomposition — PRD brief
content:
Purpose and summary:

This note outlines a concept for letting tenants negotiate ephemeral burst capacity while keeping strict per-tenant SLAs decomposed into measurable headroom components. Goal: let teams buy or borrow short-duration capacity in a predictable, observable way, avoid noisy-neighbor fallout, and provide explicit operational handoffs when degradation occurs.

Why this idea? (problem we see)
- Customers want predictable baseline capacity but also need predictable, short bursts for launches, demos, batch spikes.
- Current naive burst schemes either (a) over-commit and cause tail latency spikes for co-tenants, or (b) rigidly isolate and waste idle GPUs.
- Operators want clear accountability and easy manual/automated fallbacks when island-level pressure grows.

High-level approach
- Decompose SLA into three measurable tokens: latency budget, throughput headroom, and warm-instance reservation.
- Introduce a short-lived "Burst Reserve" instrument (BR) that a tenant can request/commit to: a small guaranteed slice of capacity for X minutes at a defined cost or a borrowable credit that decays.
- A bidding/negotiation flow: tenant can (i) purchase pre-committed BRs, (ii) request ad-hoc BRs that the system grants subject to global headroom and auction rules, or (iii) borrow against a grace credit balance for emergency bursts.
- Isolation boundary: granted BRs get QoS tokens mapped into a per-tenant serving shim (soft cgroup-like limits, KV-cache affinity, and eviction priority) to reduce cross-tenant interference.

User stories
- As an engineering manager, I want to schedule a 15-minute burst for a marketing demo that guarantees 95th-pct latency <= 200ms for N concurrent calls, so my demo doesn’t flake.
- As a platform engineer, I want to set tenant defaults for burst borrowing and a maximum daily burst spend cap so we avoid runaway costs.
- As an SRE, I want clear signal and automated remediation if aggregate BR usage breaches cluster thermal or power thresholds.

Key concepts and definitions
- BR (Burst Reserve): token representing guaranteed slices for a bounded time window. Has attributes: duration, GPU fraction, priority tier, cost type (prepaid vs borrow).
- Grace Credit: an account-level credit that allows immediate borrowing at higher cost and with automatic fallback/eviction rules. Credits decay exponentially to encourage conservative use.
- SLA decomposition: split SLO for a tenant into (latency headroom, throughput headroom, warm pool). Each BR consumes from these buckets distinctively.
- QoS shim: low-latency enforcement layer between router and runtime that enforces per-tenant KV-cache residency hints, GPU concurrency caps, and scheduling priority for gradient of fairness.

Requirements (must-have)
- API: POST /tenants/{id}/burst-reserve to request BRs; GET /tenants/{id}/burst-status; DELETE /tenants/{id}/burst-reserve/{id}. Open docs plus SDK wrappers.
- Accounting: precise per-request attribution of tokens consumed during BR windows; billing exportable to billing pipeline hourly.
- Enforcement: BR grants must map to runtime resource reservations (fractional GPU slots, pinned KV cache quotas, or reserved prewarmed instances). If hardware-level reservation not possible, fallback to strictly higher priority scheduling and prefetched KV-cache segments.
- Safety: a global cluster safety gate that rejects or delays new BR grants when thermal/energy/operational thresholds (thermal dispatch, GPU mem pressure, slot saturation) exceed safe limits.

Non-functional requirements
- Latency overhead from QoS shim must be < 0.5ms p50 added to path.
- Accounting precision: token attribution error <= 0.5% at 95th percentile across 1-hour windows.
- Rollout flagging: feature should be togglable per-organization for gradual rollout.

Design options considered (tradeoffs)
1) Hard reservations (dedicated fractional GPU lanes) vs soft guarantees (priority scheduling + KV hints)
   - Hard reservations: predictable but can waste cycles and increase costs. Complex for mixed-architecture pools.
   - Soft guarantees: efficient but riskier under contention; needs robust eviction/fallback.
   - Proposal: hybrid: allow hard reservations for paid precommitted BRs; soft guarantees for ad-hoc borrowing.
2) Auction model vs simple quota queueing
   - Auction: efficient allocation of scarce burst headroom (price discovery) but more complex UX and edge cases around price spikes.
   - Quota queueing: simpler and predictable, but can lead to lower utilization.
   - Proposal: start with priority-based queueing + dynamic pricing signals; iterate toward simple sealed-bid auctions if utilization warrants.

APIs and UX notes
- UX flows: schedule burst (time window + desired concurrency + max spend), immediate borrow (one-click emergency), and auto-refresh/extend with guardrails.
- Console: visual timeline of BRs, with color-coded state (granted, queued, declined, throttled) and predicted impact on tenant SLOs.
- Alerts: tenant-level Slack/email notifications for grant/decline and when falls back to soft guarantees. Link to runbook.

Telemetry and metrics (for decisions & alerting)
- BR_grants_count, BR_denials_count, BR_active_seconds_by_tenant, BR_consumed_gpu_fraction
- Per-tenant latency delta during BR windows (p50/p95/p99) vs baseline
- Cross-tenant interference index (derived signal) to trigger global safety gate
- Thermal pressure gauge: cluster-level metric feeding into safety gate

Operational runbook (sketch)
- Normal ops: automated allocation; billing reconciles at hour boundary.
- On safety gate trips: reject new BRs, notify on-call SRE, throttle low-priority BRs, and optionally drain opportunistic workloads.
- Emergency eviction: follow eviction policy ordered by (borrowed vs prepaid) -> (priority tier) -> (age). Publish eviction notices 30s before hard-evict when possible.

Billing and economics
- Two price planes: prepaid BR (discounted) and borrow BR (premium surge pricing); both appear on hourly statement.
- Support per-tenant daily cap and hard stop to prevent cost surprises. Admin console to increase caps for one-off events.

Testing and experiments
- Stage 1: Simulation run using historical traffic traces (prod anonymous sampling) to model collision scenarios and tuning credit decay policies.
- Stage 2: Canary with small set of tenants (opt-in) using soft guarantees only; monitor interference index and user-experience signal.
- Stage 3: Introduce prepaid hard reservations for beta tenants and compare.

Rollout plan
- Month 0–1: design + infra prototypes (accounting, API endpoints, simulated scheduler).
- Month 2–3: run cluster simulations + internal dogfood with platform team; iterate enforcement shim.
- Month 4: public beta for select customers; collect qualitative feedback.
- Month 6: GA with pricing, docs, and runbook.

Open questions / decision log
- Q: What should be the minimum BR duration that makes hard reservations feasible?
  A: Ops viewpoint: >= 5 minutes to amortize allocation overhead. Need experiments.
- Q: Should grace credits be transferrable between teams within an org?
  A: Initially no — complexity and billing confusion; consider later.
- Q: Auction UX complexity vs adoption friction?
  A: Start simple and surface price signals; revisit auctions if utilization remains low.

Next steps / action items
- Product: finalize API contract + console mockups (owner: Ava) — due 2025-10-10.
- Infra: prototype QoS shim and per-tenant attribution (owner: Diego) — spike due 2025-09-26.
- SRE: define thermal safety gate thresholds and integrate monitoring (owner: Liam) — due 2025-10-03.
- Finance: propose pricing bands for prepaid vs borrow (owner: Priya) — due 2025-10-08.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep BR naming compact in UI ("Burst slot — 15m") and show estimated impact on SLOs.
- Link this doc to capacity-sim-runbook and warm-pool-costing spreadsheet (WIP).
- Slack threads: #dedicated-burst, #infra-burst-ops.

Appendix (short): examples
- Example: tenant A schedules 10-minute BR for 5 GPU-fractions at 11:00 UTC. System grants prepaid BR: scheduler pins 2 warm instances and marks KV-cache residency; observed p95 latency improves by 30% for that window. Billing: apportioned line item for prepaid BR.
- Example borrow: tenant B hits traffic spike; borrows 3 BR slots from grace credit; system grants soft-guarantee with higher priority scheduling; after 7 minutes, cluster thermal gate triggers and tenant B is partially throttled; fall back to cheaper model variant enabled automatically.

This remains an early, intentionally pragmatic design. Feedback welcome — especially around the billing UX and the eviction notice tradeoffs.
